mappings.note: What the Keeling curve shows: rising atmospheric CO2 from human activity. POOR FIT - the frame has no outcome for anthropogenic carbon, and this is recall of a named graph's content rather than building or reading a model, so C8.1 would overstate it.

Reads a slope-vs-valley temperature table at 2 PM and predicts a valley breeze. LO-5 holds both halves - the differential heating and the named breeze - which is why no sibling can separate this from the diagram and prose versions of the same item.

Northern-hemisphere gyres turning clockwise. POOR FIT: the mechanism is the Earth's rotation acting on the ocean, and this frame has an outcome for neither. Only the competency's mention of the hydrosphere keeps it legal.

Diagram of daytime upslope circulation, to be named as a valley breeze. LO-5 names it. Shares the outcome with O17, O31, V70 and S112 - an honest family, because LO-5 is the only outcome that mentions breezes at all.

The consequence of weaker gravity is losing the atmosphere, so the item hinges on the atmosphere being a retained sphere - LO-55 names it. POOR FIT on the cause: gravity appears nowhere in this frame.

Equatorial warmth vs polar cold because the rays strike perpendicularly at the equator and are spread at the poles. Latitude and curvature are LO-4's own words. Not LO-5: no surface property and no atmospheric phenomenon is asked for.
Identifies the denitrifying group from a reactant/product table. Microbial roles in the nitrogen cycle, C4.3. Not LO-56: the table is supplied, and the student produces no flow chart.

POOR FIT and a finding. The item recalls which treaty banned CFCs - environmental policy and international cooperation, for which this frame has NO outcome. C5.3/CG5 ('linkages... across other curricular areas') is the only legal code that reaches outside science.

Combustion consuming oxygen and releasing CO2 - the abiotic arm of the oxygen cycle, and a human perturbation of it. C2.8 by my rule that human/geological perturbation goes to the competency. Not C4.3: no organism performs this reaction.

Two of the three statements are atmospheric structure (lapse rate, tropopause height), which no outcome covers, hence C2.8. The third is ozone absorbing UV - the one mechanism present, and that is LO-3's band-selective absorption.

Why the colder, saltier mass sinks. POOR FIT: density-driven deep circulation, purely hydrosphere, with no radiation or heating mechanism the outcomes can attach to. Grouped with O16 and S101 under the competency for the same reason.

Picks the correct N2 to ammonia to nitrite to nitrate order. A sequence selected from options, not a flow chart produced, so C4.3 and not LO-56 - the same line that sends S107, L123 and N9 the other way.

Finds the false water-cycle statement; the error is infiltration confused with run-off, a geosphere/hydrosphere distinction. The frame's only water-cycle toehold is LO-5's word 'evaporation', which this item does not test, so the competency carries it alone.

Sub-tropical highs form where poleward-moving air sinks - air movement from differential heating (LO-5) - and the item pins it to 30 degrees N and S, which is latitude (LO-4). Both clauses are genuinely exercised.

Nitrate, dissolved-oxygen and fish-mortality columns to be read as eutrophication. The dependent variable is a population, so C4.3; C2.8 carries the agricultural cause. Same pairing as O9, O19, S97 and C136.

The Gulf Stream keeping ports ice-free is heat redistribution driven by differential heating (LO-5), carried by the ocean (C2.8). Separated from O16/O40, which are about density and salinity rather than heat transport.

The ocean as a carbon reservoir regulating atmospheric CO2 - a hydrosphere/atmosphere exchange. No outcome covers the carbon cycle's abiotic reservoirs; C4.3 is withheld because no organism appears in the correct option.

Names the processes at two positions of a SUPPLIED flow chart. I hold LO-56 for items where the student produces the representation; here the chart is stimulus and the demand is knowing nitrification from denitrification, which is C4.3.

POOR FIT and a finding. Mission LiFE statements to be judged - an environmental policy initiative and its launch venue. No outcome in this frame covers policy, lifestyle or international initiatives; C5.3 is the nearest legal code.

Definition of insolation: how much of the Sun's radiation reaches the surface. LO-2's 'nature of solar radiation'. Not LO-3: the distractors are about reflection and re-radiation, not about frequency bands.

The item is about what a computer MODEL couples - C8.1's 'develops models to represent real-life events and use these models to predict results' - and the coupled quantities are the atmosphere, ocean, land and ice, i.e. the spheres (LO-55).
Matched-pair recall about atmospheric layers, which have no outcome (C2.8); the correct pair is the stratosphere with the ozone layer, and ozone's job is band-selective UV absorption (LO-3).

Names Rhizobium and Azotobacter. Organism-level recall inside the nitrogen cycle, C4.3. Nothing in the item is a diagram, a sequence or a human impact, so it takes the bare competency for the biological family.

Clouds' dual role is reflecting incoming sunlight AND absorbing outgoing surface heat - two different bands (LO-3) interacting with radiation the surface re-radiated (LO-5). The 'other function' asked for is specifically the infrared half.

Asks which reservoir is NOT in the fast cycle; the answer is fossil fuels, a geosphere store (C2.8), and the three distractors are the biotic fast-cycle reservoirs (C4.3). The item is scored on the fast/slow boundary, so both are needed.
